successCriteria.description: The controller class exposes exactly 8 public async methods — createDraft, submit, approve, reject, cancel, findById, findByEmployeeId, query — each mapping 1:1 to the corresponding ILeaveRequestService method signature.
Every controller method returns a plain object with all Date fields serialized as ISO 8601 strings; nullable Date fields (approvedAt, cancelledAt) serialize as null when absent.
The routes plugin registers all 8 endpoints with correct HTTP status codes: 201 for createDraft, 200 for all other success responses, 404 for not-found results from findById.

Service errors with a known code are mapped to the correct HTTP status: 400 for INVALID_DATE_RANGE/MINIMUM_NOTICE_VIOLATION, 403 for NOT_MANAGER, 404 for EMPLOYEE_NOT_FOUND/POLICY_NOT_FOUND/REQUEST_NOT_FOUND/BALANCE_NOT_FOUND, 409 for INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION/INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE/BALANCE_CLOSED/POLICY_INACTIVE, 500 for unrecognized errors.
Error response bodies conform to the shape { error: string; code: string } for known errors, and { error: 'Internal Server Error' } (no code field) for unexpected errors.
The route file registers GET /leave-requests/employee/:employeeId before GET /leave-requests/:id to avoid the employeeId path segment being captured as an :id parameter.
The routes plugin is registered in src/app.ts via app.register(leaveRequestRoutes).

Jest tests use Fastify's inject() method with a mocked ILeaveRequestService, covering all 8 endpoints with at least one happy-path and one error case each, and verifying status codes and error body shapes.

constraints: The controller constructor MUST accept ILeaveRequestService (not the concrete LeaveRequestService) — the controller depends on the interface, enabling testability via mocking.
The routes plugin MUST be a named async function export (not a default export) so it can be registered with app.register().
No RBAC middleware is wired at the HTTP layer in this phase — manager authorization for approve/reject is enforced at the service layer only. RBAC guards are deferred to a later phase.
No audit logging or notification dispatch is triggered from the controller or routes — these cross-cutting concerns are deferred to Phase 10.
The controller must not import or depend on Fastify types (FastifyRequest, FastifyReply, etc.) — it is a plain TypeScript class that receives already-extracted values from the route handlers.
outOfScope: RBAC middleware (GP-005) wired at the HTTP layer — routes accept all requests without auth guards in this phase.
Notification dispatch on leave lifecycle transitions — not integrated; deferred to Phase 10.
